findings.text: Upheld as advisory (question 4/9). The perSentence guard's ': 0' arm is reached only by a unit test, because rejudge's asInput always sends candidates: []. It keeps the DistillInput.wording contract consistent, so it is not a dead path.

Upheld as advisory (question 9). The check result.verdict?.source !== judge.name cannot be true once readingOf has returned 'emptied' for a turn with no candidates. It is kept as an AC-11 safeguard (TypeSafe verdicts only).
Upheld as advisory (question 2). buildDraft sorts known with surestFirst twice, at lines 133 and 138. One sorted array would serve both. This is boilerplate-sized.
Upheld as advisory (question 8). PreparedTexts and TurnTexts (line 254) are exported, but nothing imports them by name.
Upheld as advisory (question 6). One header comment line runs past the wrapping of the lines around it. Style only.

Lowered to advisory as debt: the diff did not write this line. hasDurable still uses a hard-coded 0.5 while KNOWLEDGE_THRESHOLD is 0.45, so a sentence scoring 0.45 to 0.5 can count as knowledge in buildDraft while the turn's worth stays capped.

Upheld as advisory (AC-5, question 1; mutant reasoned about, not run). The mostly-report discount is proven only on answers that are all report. Raising REPORT_SHARE from 0.6 to 1.0 would survive. One 3-of-5 case would pin the 'mostly' boundary.

Upheld as advisory (AC-5, question 6). probes/report-discount-removed.txt shows this test still passing with REPORT_DISCOUNT removed: its result comes from the !hasDurable cap, not from the discount its name claims. The criterion stays proven by line 398.

Upheld as advisory (AC-1/AC-11, question 1). The report's per-pattern drop line and its 'Quoted candidates the filter dropped' section are never asserted. Each drop is proven at the filter level in tests/unit/noise.test.ts, so only the report's wording is unpinned.

Upheld as advisory (AC-4, question 2, partial). The replaying judge looks answers up by turn id, so changing the version 2 instructions would not force a re-recording. The wording is pinned separately in tests/unit/questions.test.ts:32-40. This is about how fresh the recording is, not about the criterion.
Lowered to advisory as debt, outside the change: the withFallback stubs still declare typesafe version '1'. Harmless to this item.

Upheld as advisory (question 4, personal-data). The default labeller is the runtime's own agent, so the sampled turn text reaches that model's provider. The brief states this, and --projects/--exclude-projects narrow the draw. The header claim in quality.ts:10-11 covers only the script. This is a choice the author makes, not a send by the code to a broader audience.

Upheld as advisory (question 4, retention/erasure). The work-dir copy of the whole store is outside forget/compact. Deletion by hand is stated (quality.sh:22-25, ADR 0023:21) and umask 077 applies. A reminder at the end of the run would be hardening.

Upheld as advisory (question 1, hardening). A work dir containing a single quote breaks sqlite3's .backup dot-command. Only the author passes this argument, and the live database is opened -readonly, so no caller path crosses a boundary.

Upheld as advisory (question 1). The three skip reasons write the same 'skipped' state with no counter. The spec states this risk (spec:299), the proof measures the filter's and the judge's losses on the real store before release, and fewer memories show in the viewer. That is a way to see it, so this is not the rubric's 'failure nobody would see'. A drain-side counter would make the first hour safer, which is advisory.

Upheld as advisory (question 2/5). Rolling back does not re-distil turns that v2 skipped, and recovery rests on the undesigned D-1 inside compact's 90-day window. The spec and ADR 0023:22 state the dependency and its window, so it is a stated, manual rollback, not an unstated dependency.

Upheld as advisory (question 1). stripHost can cut the rest of a final answer at an unclosed host tag that opens a line outside a fence, and the live drain records nothing. The proof counts it (1 turn on B). Nothing is deleted from the store: the turn text stays.
Upheld as advisory (question 6). Deleting the work-dir store copy is a manual step that is named but has no owner and no reminder at the end of a measure run.
Lowered to advisory as debt, outside the change: turns has never recorded why a turn was skipped.
Lowered to advisory as debt, outside the change: compact's 90-day text window existed before this item.

Upheld as advisory (question 3). The doc comments on durable and titleIdx still give the version 1 meanings. Spec section 7 and ADR 0023 declare that the field names are kept, so this is not undeclared drift. Reword the comments.

Upheld as advisory (question 5). Spec section 8 places the decision rules in policy.ts, but buildDraft in pipeline.ts applies them. buildDraft already lived there, so no boundary is crossed. Move the rules, or reword section 8.

Upheld as advisory (question 6). Exports used only by the proof (storedDetail, toldInSession, unfilteredTexts, and heuristicJudgeV1, which the reviewer placed at heuristic.ts:869 but which is at src/judge/heuristic.ts:256) widen src/'s surface. This matches the precedent of scripts/proof/moments.ts.
Lowered to advisory as debt: the SQL inside toldInSession in the distill layer predates the change; the diff only added bounds to it.
Upheld as advisory (question 2). The correlated NOT EXISTS over memories has no covering index. It is an offline query on a copy, never on a hook or drain path, so the cost is time only.
Upheld as advisory (question 1). openDb migrates the work-dir copy. The live store is only read (sqlite3 -readonly .backup), so 'read-only' in AC-11 describes the live store, not the copy.
Upheld as advisory (question 5). Retention of the work dir's copy and samples is stated as deletion by hand, behind umask 077 and a location guard. Erasure depends on the author remembering.
Lowered to advisory as debt, outside the change: injections_once is partial, so toldInSession's filter on session_id alone scans injections. That predates this item.
